main_text.l: قوله ﻣﻜﻦ وبعضه في ﻣﺤﻞ ﻛﺎﻻﻣﺮ والنهي والخبر والاسﻢ [?] خبار partim non in subjecto, ut dictum ejus, كن
Esto [scil. in creatione rerum] & partim in
subjecto ut mandatum, & Prohibitio, & Narratio, &
Interrogatio, &c. Idem etiam Alfobbaiensem, (qui &
apud Motazalos lectæ princeps) asseruisse ait, loqui
Deum بكلام مخلوق في محل Sermone quem creat in
subjecto, scil. (ut explicat Author libri AlMawakef, كاللوح المحفوظ او جبريل
او النبي in tabula[in coelis] repofita, in Gabriele, in Propheta, &c. Contra
AlMotazalos hac de re disputant qui se pro Ortho-
doxis haberi volunt verbum Dei nec voce & literis
consistere, nec creatum & in subjecto esse conten-
dentes, differentiâ tamen, quæ & Authori libri M-
awakef, ejusque expositori videtur, conciliari possit
adhibita distinctione verbi in كلاما لفظيا verbum
prolatum, & الدعني القا يم بالنفس signficationem seu
intentionem in mente subsistentem, seu permanentem:
seu in الغنسي mentale, seu mente conceptum, &
الافظي Sermone prolatum, seu orale.
E Motazalis autem Ahmed Ebn Hayet asseruit
Christum corpus proprie dictum induisse, &c.] Hunc
cum e secta AlNodamianorum (qui ab Abrahamo
AlNodham denominati sunt) fuerat, postea
novam sibi, novarum post lectos Philosophorum
libros opinionum accessione condidisse, qui ab
ipso AlHayetiani dicti sunt, refert AlSharesta-
niu, atque idem asseruisse ipsum cum Christianis في اعتقادهم ان المسيح هو النبي محاسب nis الخلق

page.notes: Arabic text is hard to read in places: the word after "والاسم" on the second line and several words in the Arabic lines are uncertain and marked [?] or left as read. The Arabic line ending "nis الخلق" has a Latin fragment "nis" inside the Arabic line, copied as printed. The note "v. Sharko Ta-wakea" is also uncertain in its spelling. The printed square bracket after "induisse, &c." is left as printed.
